items.title: 3.6.1 Molecular orbital diagrams of some diatomic molecules and their bond orders

source_refs.note: Topic 3.6.1, printed pages 65-67 (Figures 3.36 to 3.38). The print's 'figure 36' for oxygen is Figure 3.38; its oxygen bond order is printed as '2( )' with the fraction lost.

blocks.text: The configuration of He is 1s2. For He2 to form, the 1s orbitals of two helium atoms must combine into a bonding sigma 1s and an antibonding sigma* 1s orbital. Of the four electrons, two enter the bonding orbital and the remaining two the antibonding orbital, so the bond order of He2 is (2 - 2) / 2 = 0; hence the He2 molecule is not formed.

Nitrogen is 1s2 2s2 2px1 2py1 2pz1. The valence 2s orbitals of the two atoms give sigma 2s and sigma* 2s, while the 2p orbitals give six molecular orbitals in increasing order of energy: sigma 2s < sigma* 2s < pi 2py = pi 2pz < sigma 2px < pi* 2py = pi* 2pz < sigma* 2px. The bond order of N2 from its diagram is (6 - 0) / 2 = 3, so there are three covalent bonds between the nitrogen atoms, one sigma and two pi: a triple bond.

For oxygen the energies of the molecular orbitals are arranged sigma 2s < sigma* 2s < sigma 2px < pi 2py = pi 2pz < pi* 2py = pi* 2pz < sigma* 2px. The bond order of oxygen is 2, which shows one sigma and one pi bond between the oxygen atoms, a double bond O=O. The oxygen molecule is paramagnetic: it is attracted by a magnetic field, and liquid oxygen is attracted and suspended between the poles of a strong magnet. Paramagnetic substances have one or more unpaired electrons, and a substance with many unpaired electrons is strongly paramagnetic. MOT explains this behaviour: the MO diagram of oxygen shows two unpaired electrons, one each in pi* 2py and pi* 2pz, which give the molecule a net magnetic field that interacts with an external field.

blocks.alt: An energy diagram. Each helium atom has a 1s orbital with two electrons. They combine into a lower bonding orbital, sigma 1s, and a higher antibonding orbital, sigma* 1s, each holding two electrons. A box gives bond order = (2 - 2) / 2 = 0, so He2 does not exist.
blocks.caption: Molecular orbital diagram of the He2 molecule (original diagram after Figure 3.36).

blocks.alt: An energy diagram for N2. Each nitrogen has 2s2 2p3. In the molecule, from the bottom: sigma 2s (2 electrons), sigma* 2s (2), the two pi 2p orbitals (4), sigma 2px (2), then empty pi* 2p and sigma* 2px. Bond order = (8 - 2) / 2 = 3, a triple bond with all electrons paired.
blocks.caption: Molecular orbital diagram of the N2 molecule (original diagram after Figure 3.37).

blocks.alt: An energy diagram for O2. Each oxygen has 2s2 2p4. In the molecule, from the bottom: sigma 2s (2), sigma* 2s (2), sigma 2px (2), the two pi 2p orbitals (4), then one electron in each pi* 2p orbital, and sigma* 2px empty. Bond order = (8 - 4) / 2 = 2; the two unpaired electrons make O2 paramagnetic.
blocks.caption: Molecular orbital diagram of the O2 molecule (original diagram after Figure 3.38).
